traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Gymnosperms (DELTA, 2008 onwards, version of 5 August 2019), Welwitschiaceae: a long-lived woody plant whose short unbranched stem, on a taproot, widens into a disc up to a metre across and bears only two (rarely three) strap-shaped leaves; they grow from their bases all the plant's life and spread over the ground, fraying at the tips; veins nearly parallel.
